seoMeta.title: Whitepapers — XGD
seoMeta.description: Two papers on generative development: the structural wall AI-assisted projects run into, and XGD — a governor built to get past it, reported over nine months of building itself.

config.successMessage: On their way — check your inbox.

children.text: The first makes the case that generative development runs into a structural wall, and that no better model removes it. The second describes what we built instead, and reports nine months of using it to build itself.
One frames the problem. One answers it.
Both are written for people building real systems this way, not for a general audience. They assume you have hit some of this yourself.
How Can You Trust the Code Your AI Writes?

Four waves of AI-assisted development, and the wall the third one runs into. Why the problem is structural rather than a limit of model capability, what better models will and won’t fix, and the case for behavioural identity — an explicit, maintained record of what software is supposed to do. Introduces the Software Artificer.

The companion paper. XGD as a governor for generative development: the Capability Matrix as target state, automated agentic engineering as the correction mechanism, and the Artificer’s control surface. Reports nine months of building XGD with XGD — the velocity, the regression rate, and what we still don’t know.
Both papers are free. We ask for an email because that is how we send them — a link to each, straight back. We will only use your address to email you about XGD.
We’ll send a link to each paper. The beta waitlist is separate — you can join that any time from the home page.
